Let $Z(f)$ (the zero set of $f$ ) be the set of all $p \in X$ at which $f(p)=0$. Prove that $Z(f)$ is closed.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "real_analysis", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Since \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\) and the continuous map \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) has closed preimages of closed sets, \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). Moreover,
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed."}
